 F. GENERAL FUND RESERVES

  Purpose:
  The purpose of this policy is to establish guidelines for the General Fund’s unrestncted kind balance
  to improve and maintain the City’s financial stability in order to protect the City from unforeseen or
  unbudgeted situations (e.g. natural disasters, major infrastructure failures, unexpected litigation).

  Background:
  Fund balance serves as a measure of the financial resources available in a governmental kind. It is
  essential that governments maintain adequate levels of fund balance to mitigate current and future
  risks (e.g. revenue shortfalls and unanticipated expenditures) and to ensure stable tax rates.

  In February 2009, the Governmental Accounting Standards Board issued GASB Statement No. 54,
  Fettid Balance Reporting and Governmental Fund Type Definitions, which separates lund balance
  into five separate categories based on the type and source of constraints placed on how resources can
  be spent. Presented in descending order from most constraining to least constraining, they include:
  nonspendable kind balance, restricted hind balance, committed kind balance, assigned fund balance,
  and unassigned fund balance. The total amounts in the last three categories (where the only constraint
  on spending, if any, is imposed by the govenunent itself) is termed unrestricted lund balance. GASB
  Statement No. 54 recommends  “..  at a minimum, that general-purpose governments, regardless of
  size, niainta in unrestric ted lund balance in their general fund of no less than two months of regula r
  general fund operating revenues or regular general fund operating expenditures. The choice of
  revenues or expenditures as a basis of comparison may be dictated by what is more predictable in a
  government’s particular circumstances.”

  The adequacy of unrestricted kind balance in the General Fund should take into account the City’s
  unique circumstances and the City should consider the following factors to assess the adequacy of
  unrestricted hind balance:
  • Predictability of its revenues and volatility of its expenditures;
  • Perceived exposure to significant one-time outlays;
  • Potential drain upon General Fund resources from other kinds, as well as the availability of
  resources in other hinds;
  • Potential impact on the entity’s bond ratings and the corresponding increased cost of borrowed
  finds;
  • Commitments and assignments included in the unrestricted fund balance

  Policy:
  The City of Avalon will stnve to maintain an unrestricted fund balance equal to no less than six (6)
  months of regular General Fund operating expenditure budget. The regular operating expenditure
  budget includes all current operating expenditure appropriations, excluding capital outlays and other
  one-time discretionary payments.

  Visitor-driven tax revenues (e.g. transient occupancy tax, sales tax, admission tax) account for the
  majority of the City’s General Fund revenues, with the predictability of these revenues dependent on

  165
 overall tourism demand. Due to its unique location, City revenues are particularly vulnerable to
disruptions to leisure travel and tourism caused by pandemics or other natural disasters. In addition,
the City is responsible for managing multiple enterprise kinds, with operating expenditures
comparable in size to its General Fund, and the City needs to maintain reserves in order to cover
immediate capital needs, if working capital is not sufficient in those kinds.

Funds appropriated from unrestricted kind balance should bc appropriated for non-recurring
expenditures, as they represent prior year surpluses that may or may not materialize in subsequent
years. However, draws from unrestricted kind balance below the six month target amount or to cover
recurring operating costs are generally reserved for emergency or unibreseen situations but may be
accessed by Council by simple budget appropriation. Examples of situations may include but not
limited to the following:
  A. Sudden and unexpected significant thdiity failure that presents an immediate public safety
  concern to the community;
  B. Declaration of a State of Emergency by the Governor;
  C. Unanticipated expenditures as a result of legislative changes from State/Federal governments
  in the current fiscal year;
  D. Acts of Terrorism declared by the Governor or the President of the United States;
  E. Acts of nature, which are infrequent in occurrence; or
  F. Other emergency as defined by City Council

If unrestricted fund balance is to he used to kind recurring operating expenditures or if unrestricted
kind balance falls below the minimum threshold, the Finance Director shall recommend and submit
to City Council a plan to replenish reserves to minimum levels. This plan will specil’ the source of
funding and timeframe for replenishment. Reserves should be replenished within three years, if
possible.

Policy

and Solid Waste Collection System in a manner that will provide maximum security for the City’s
capital, while also meeting the cash flow needs of the City relative to its participalion in
CalRecycle’s Solid Waste Postclosure and Corrective Action Trust Fund (“State Trust Fund”).
This policy confomis to all state and local law governing the investment of public finds and aims
to maximize return within an acceptable and defined level of risk.

Scope
This investment policy applies to the City’s establishment of a trust fluid for landfill closure and
postclosure costs (‘focal Trust Fund”) in compliance with CalRecyele’s Snue Trust Fund
program, as well as to cover corrective action and operating liabilities. This policy is intended to
supplement and not rephce any other City investment pohcies for general operations or other
specified purposes.

Delegation of Authority
The City Treasurer has been authorized to undertake investment transactions on behalf of the City.

Safekeeping of Securities
In accordance with Government Code Section 53601. aU securities owned by the City shall be
held in safekeeping by the City’s custodial bank or a third party bank trust department, acting for
the City under the terms of a custody agreement. All securities will be received arid delivered
using standard Delivery Versus Payment procedures. which ensures that securities are deposited
with the third party custodian prior to release of hinds. A third party custodian as evidenced by
safekeeping receipts will hold securities. Investments in LAIF or money market mutual hinds are
undeliverable and are not subject to delivery or third party safekeeping.

Diversification
The City will diversify its investments by security type and institution. With the exception of US
Treasury securities and authorized pools WAIF and LACIP). no more than SO% of the entity’s
total investment portfolio will he invested in a single secunty type or with a single financial
institution.

Maximum Maturities
To the extent possible. the City will attempt to match its investments with anticipated cash flow
requirements. Unless matched to a specific cash flow and authorized by the Government Code,
the City will not directly invest in securities matured more than five (5) years from the dale of
purchase.

Internal Control
The Treasurer shall establish an annual process of independent review by an external auditor.
This review will provide assurances on internal controls throuith compliance with policies arid
proccdures.

Perfoniiancc Standards
The investment portfolio will be designed to obtain the highest rate, with the greatest security
and liquidity consistent with the cash flow requirements of the City, but at no less rate oil the
date of investment than the rate being paid by the Local Agency Investment Fund (LAIF).
